name: Your own hub page
summary: The best home for every link. You own it, so it isn't subject to anyone else's posting rules, and the disclosure is built in.
notes: Share the hub URL from other places instead of individual referral links where you can.
Rakuten's terms specifically allow links on pages you own and control.

name: Friends and family, directly
summary: Where EDF's and Starling's terms intend their links to be used.
notes: Send a link to people you know who would genuinely benefit.
Tell them it's your referral link and what you get.

name: r/beermoneyuk
summary: The biggest UK side-income sub, and the one you already use. Referral posts are allowed with conditions.
notes: Include a non-referral link alongside your referral link or code, clearly labelled. Hiding a referral link behind a non-referral link gets a ban.
Name the site in the post title, give the steps to qualify, and mention any credit check.
Offers must be available in the UK.
Reposting the same site has a cooldown, and the figures I found disagree (5 days, once a month, 14 days). Check the live wiki and set the number in the tracker.
I couldn't find a rule restricting some apps to admins. Confirm with the mods if unsure.
My source was a third-party mirror of the wiki, which may be out of date.

name: r/UK_Referral_Codes
summary: A small sub made for sharing UK codes and links.
notes: Its rule is not to repeat the same link within 7 days.
Small (about 4k members), so expect low reach.
Read the sidebar for current rules before posting.

name: r/Referralsuk
summary: Small sub for honest UK referral offers with clear rewards, conditions and rotation rules.
notes: Bans spam and fake claims, so state both sides and the conditions clearly (your cards already do).
About 2k members, so low reach.

name: r/DiscountCodesUK
summary: UK discount and voucher codes. Referral posts appear but are a minority.
notes: Mostly retail codes, so only your shopping-type offers (Klarna, Rakuten) are likely to fit.
Check the sidebar rules first.

name: X (Twitter)
summary: Free to post by hand. Automating it is no longer free for new developers.
notes: Start the post with a clear "Ad" label. UK rules treat referral links as adverts and want the label up front, not buried.
X bans automated spam and scripting the website can get an account suspended. Posting identical content repeatedly is treated as manipulation.
The old free API tier is closed to new developers. Sources suggest pay-per-use credits, with link posts costing noticeably more. Check X's developer pages.
Use the "Short version" in the tracker's Compose tab, and post it yourself.

name: Bluesky
summary: Free to post, and its API is free to use, but the UK money audience is small.
notes: Same "Ad" label rule applies.
If you ever automate, Bluesky's docs recommend labelling the account as a bot and respecting rate limits. Its guidelines ban repeated spam.
My source was vendor blogs, so check Bluesky's own docs.

name: Mastodon
summary: Free, and it supports scheduled posts, but each server sets its own rules and the audience is small.
notes: Read your server's rules on promotion before posting.
Same "Ad" label rule applies.

name: EasyEarns
summary: A UK referral marketplace where submissions are reviewed before they go live.
notes: Run by a company, and the only review evidence I found was two Trustpilot reviews. Read its terms and what it does with your links before using it.
Check each provider's terms allow listing your link on a third-party site.

name: Share My Link
summary: A newer UK platform for finding and sharing referral codes and cashback offers (launched April 2026).
notes: I found no independent reviews, so treat it as unproven.
Check each provider's terms allow listing your link on a third-party site.

name: MoneySavingExpert forum
summary: Staff have said members shouldn't share referral codes or links.
notes: Posting referral links publicly risks a ban.
Some people share by private message, but that's a grey area. Don't rely on it.

name: HotUKDeals
summary: Its community rules treat referral links and requests for referrals as spam.
notes: Don't post referral links in threads.

name: Overclockers UK forums
summary: Referral codes are only allowed when someone asks for them. Unprompted posting risks suspension.
notes: Only reply with a code if a member has asked for one.
